reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the orders and refunds data against the handoff from Alpha Co, so I'll start by listing the orders.
Alpha Co says refunds for orders 140, 144, and 145 were applied, so I'll check the refunds ledger against that handoff before computing any payouts.
The refunds ledger matches Alpha Co's handoff exactly (orders 140, 144, 145). Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 38617 matches its orders (17469 + 27956) minus its refund on order 140 (6808). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 35795 matches its orders (21876 + 33383) minus its refund on order 144 (19464). Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.
All three net balances match the orders minus the refunds, and the refunds ledger matches Alpha Co's handoff, so there's no reason to hold. I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 38617 was recorded successfully. Next I'll record birch's payout of 35795, which matches its net balance.
Cobalt's net balance of 11416 matches its orders (8761 + 12156) minus its refund on order 145 (9501), and the earlier checks passed, so I'll record cobalt's payout.

All three payouts are recorded. Each amount matches its net balance, and I checked each one against orders minus refunds: acme 45425 - 6808 = 38617, birch 55259 - 19464 = 35795, cobalt 20917 - 9501 = 11416. No customers were missed, and no orders were left without a matching refund.
